A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EraseBench study despite the changed title. Their main text, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, added, and removed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-erasure experiments, CLIP/Gecko/RAHF measurements, qualitative analyses, and an 11-participant human preference study.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds explicit-concept evaluations, mitigation experiments, computational measurements, and an AdvUnlearn human preference study.

M1.justification: The benchmark retains its concept-curation approach and evaluates the same five existing erasure algorithms on Stable Diffusion. No new architecture, loss, or erasure algorithm is introduced. Retain-set, anchor, and multi-concept experiments vary evaluation configurations rather than establish a new proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluated NSFW, cultural, and safety-related cases, including nudity versus statues and firearms versus broader weapon concepts (Tables 2 and 8). Section 6 also extends single-target erasure to simultaneous erasure of related or unrelated concepts, introducing materially different task requirements.

E2.justification: The main automated comparison retains ESD, UCE, Receler, MACE, and AdvUnlearn. Human validation expands from original Stable Diffusion versus UCE alone to include original Stable Diffusion versus AdvUnlearn (v2 Section 5.3 and Appendix G). Newly cited erasure methods do not enter the main comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces harmonic-mean aggregation, controlled comparisons of absent/unrelated/related retain sets, anchor configurations, and single versus intra-type/inter-type erasure. It also adds an independently recruited AdvUnlearn human study. Appendix G reports nine new participants, but the reported 1,485 responses are not reconciled with Section 5.3's description of 50 image pairs and three questions per participant.

E4.justification: New Section 6 tests whether retain sets restore non-target concepts while causing target leakage, whether anchors prevent distortions, and whether grouping erased concepts matters. v2 also adds a Gecko object-presence error breakdown. Conversely, v1's DAAM attention-map analysis in Section 3 and Figure 2 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain ten generation seeds, uncertainty values, and pooled Wilcoxon signed-rank testing at alpha = 0.01. v2 drops the per-concept significance reporting and removes Table 1's explicit identification of its ± values as standard errors. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds efficacy/generality entries and harmonic means, explicit-concept scores, object-presence findings, mitigation outcomes, computational costs, and AdvUnlearn human preferences. Most retained CLIP, RAHF, and Gecko estimates remain unchanged. Gecko score-drop entries are corrected: AdvUnlearn's erased-concept drop changes from -28.0 to -41.0 while its 43.1 mean remains fixed (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3).

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The removed concept-entanglement section is conceptual and empirical. The added harmonic-mean reporting changes evaluation aggregation without introducing substantive formal theory.

C1.justification: Both present EraseBench, evaluate five erasure techniques, and claim that erasure damages related non-target concepts and undermines deployment reliability. The revised title and abstract emphasize these existing claims; the additional experiments principally supply supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantive interpretations of preservation versus target-leakage tradeoffs, anchors' limited effectiveness, and differences between related and unrelated multi-concept erasure. Its conclusion adds limitations concerning curated concept coverage and unresolved retain/erasure-set design. The earlier attention-overlap mechanism discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Gemini Flash for prompt construction, specifies default retain sets and empty anchors, and explains paraphrase construction for additional dimensions. Appendix F and Table 13 disclose A100-40GB hardware and runtime/memory measurements. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to the implementation of retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including SalUn, EraseAnything, SPEED, few-shot unlearning, and additional evaluation work. It removes DAAM and disentanglement references with the dedicated concept-entanglement discussion. The central positioning around non-target degradation, beyond residual-concept recovery and erasure efficacy, remains.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, with substantial rewriting of the abstract, introduction, benchmark description, and metric explanations. The standalone concept-entanglement section disappears, detailed baseline descriptions move to Appendix D, and separate Discussion and Conclusion and Limitations sections reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands to efficacy, generality, sensitivity, and harmonic-mean columns for all dimensions, substantially reducing text size. v2 adds a dimension diagram, intervention figures, AdvUnlearn preference charts, and explicit-concept and computational-cost tables. The DAAM figure is removed, while several existing examples and heatmaps move between the main text and appendix.

improvement.justification: The new mitigation experiments explain preservation-versus-leakage tradeoffs beyond v1's degradation findings, while safety-related evaluations and AdvUnlearn human preferences broaden empirical support. Corrected Gecko drops and added implementation disclosures improve accuracy and transparency. These gains are limited by sparse settings for the new interventions, unreconciled human-study counts, reduced statistical detail, and poorer legibility of the expanded Table 1.
